answer: Scaled dot-product attention is preferred in practice because it is much faster and more space-efficient than additive attention, as it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention]. The dot products are divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$ to counteract the effect of large $d_k$ values, which cause dot products to grow large in magnitude and push the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention].
question: Dot-product attention and additive attention have about the same theoretical cost. Why is scaled dot-product still preferred in practice, and why divide by √d_k when d_k is large?
